$comment: Workload manifest for cuccia-infra review (contract v0, docs/ai-node-consumers.md 'Registering your workload'). The image is built and pushed by the s6-amt-image GitHub Actions workflow (see amt/README.md); workload.image is the pushed digest. Keys under 'workload' mirror services/releases.json ai_worker_workloads entries; 'review' holds the extra facts the guide asks for.
name: go-go-harmoniyo-amt

workload.description: Anticipatory Music Transformer: accompaniment for a melody MIDI (/inputs/melody.mid + args.json -> /outputs/accompaniment.mid, combined.mid, report.json)

review.vram_basis: 360M-parameter GPT-2 in fp16 = 0.7 GiB weights; batch 1, 1024-token context, no KV cache; plus CUDA context. Measured peak is written to report.json max_vram_mib on the first node run; expected well under the ~10 GiB budget.
review.expected_runtime: GPU: seconds per carol (3 forward passes per generated note, ~120 notes for a 25 s carol) plus ~10-20 s model load. CPU reference (laptop, small model): 824 s generate for a 23 s carol.

inputs.melody.mid: Standard MIDI file, every note is a melody control; <= 99 s (AMT max sequence length 100 s); a few KB
inputs.args.json: optional: top_p (0.95), seed (1), end_seconds, history_seconds (0), drop_drums (true), keep_programs (null), device

review.runtime_requirements: non-root UID 10001, read-only rootfs OK (writes only /outputs; HOME=/tmp), HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, no network, no caches mounted (weights baked into the image)

models.name: stanford-crfm/music-medium-800k
models.license_evidence: Hugging Face model card metadata 'license: apache-2.0' (checked 2026-10-24); no use restrictions in the card
models.training_data: Lakh MIDI Dataset (CC BY 4.0 dataset; the underlying MIDI files are of mixed provenance)

python_packages.torch: 2.6.0 (cu124 wheel; BSD-3-Clause; bundles NVIDIA CUDA runtime libraries under NVIDIA's redistribution terms)

review.license_review: Project-side review (ADR-0008) in spikes/s6-ai-arranging/amt/README.md and the S6 report: model and code Apache-2.0, no NC/ND terms or use restrictions; outputs are treated as AI-generated assets (CC0) with provenance and a human resemblance review.
